# Best RV power station and solar combo

There's no single best combo. It depends on whether you need to run a roof A/C. Here are three picks, plus a smaller option for weekend trips.

## If you want to run a roof A/C or boondock full-time: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. It's expandable past 12kWh.
- A 13,500 BTU A/C draws about 1,500W running, so one battery runs it for roughly 2.3 hours.
- It's heavy enough that moving it is a two-person job, and it's the priciest option once you add batteries.
- Source and "Check price" link: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/

## Best value with a built-in RV port: BLUETTI AC200L
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W, a built-in 30A RV outlet, and up to 1,200W solar input.
- It weighs about 62 lb.
- Sources: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/ and https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

## Most capacity per dollar right now: ALLPOWERS R4000
- 3,456Wh LiFePO4, 3,600W at 120V (6,000W peak), an RV outlet, and a 5-year warranty.
- It accepts up to 2,000W of solar across three 650W inputs (12–60V). You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000W.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of a fixed install than a portable unit.
- The store price is $1,499. With code EXTRA12 it's $1,319.12, but the code expires 2026-11-15. The site tested it in ALLPOWERS's cart on 2026-10-23, and checkout has the final say. ALLPOWERS usually takes one code per order.
- Returns: 30 days for unused items, but ALLPOWERS's refund page says sale items can't be returned.
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh. This is an affiliate link that opens ALLPOWERS's official US store. It costs you nothing extra, and Dealectric earns a commission.
- Details: https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh

## For weekend trips without A/C
A ~1,000Wh unit is enough for a fridge, Starlink, a laptop and a CPAP.
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024Wh, 1,000W solar input, about 28 lb) is the top overall pick for this size.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, about 23.8 lb) is lighter, but its solar input is capped at 400W.
- Source: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

## Choosing solar panels
- **Match the panels to the station's solar input limit.** Extra panel wattage beyond the limit is wasted. That's why a 400W-capped Jackery pairs with just two 200W panels.
- A 300–400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun (source 6).
- The guides I found suggest Renogy's 200W folding suitcase and Jackery SolarSaga panels for portable setups. I didn't get current prices or direct product links for them, so check the retailer pages. Renogy is listed at https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife.

## Caveats
- I couldn't get direct product links for the EcoFlow, Bluetti and Jackery units. The review pages above have price-check links, which are affiliate links.
- The sources' prices and specs conflict in places. One older comparison lists the AC200P (a different model from the AC200L) with a 700W solar limit and a 2-year warranty. Confirm specs and price on the retailer's page before buying.
- The EmergencyEnergy guide is written for Ontario, so ignore its Canadian electrical-code references. The specs still apply.
- Have a licensed electrician do any hardwired connection to your RV.

If you tell me your rig (A/C or not, 30A or 50A, how many days off-grid, roof space), I can narrow this to one station and a specific panel wattage.
